prompt:
I need the front end for Couchwise. A household app that searches across a family's streaming subscriptions and suggests films and shows that suit whoever is watching together.

Who's using it: Daniel Osei, 41, a father of two (Kofi, 7, and Ama, 11) who chooses the Friday movie for the family. He knows little about what's new and wants to avoid another 20-minute argument.

What they're doing right now: It's Friday at 6:40 pm. His mother-in-law, who dislikes loud action and can't stand crude humor, is staying for the weekend. Kofi was frightened by a scene in last month's pick, and Ama refuses anything 'for babies'. Daniel has searched for 'funny adventure, not scary, under 100 minutes' and is checking the results against what each person has already seen and what their subscriptions include. He also wants to look at a few suggestions the app came up with on its own. He needs a pick by 7:15, when the pizza arrives.

What's in the system at this point: 4 active subscriptions (two major streamers, one public-library film service, one kids' service); one rental store account with a $5.99 credit. 4 household profiles: Dad, Mom (Abena), Ama (11), Kofi (7), plus a temporary guest profile 'Grandma Efua'. Watch history: 212 titles over 2 years, 38 marked 'family night', each with ratings from whoever rated it (e.g. Kofi gave 'The Sea Beast' 'too scary' at the kraken scene). Titles carry runtime, age rating, content notes (peril, scary moments, language, crude humor), year, language, and which service has it. Current query returns 47 matches; 9 have already been seen by at least one child.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
